note: Identifier: the equipment, then what sets the option apart, then any modifiers, joined by underscores.
Plain-language name of the archetype.
Every family the archetype appears under in the workbook: its home family first, then the families of the sectors whose end uses it serves.
The end uses (hierarchy service nodes) the archetype serves.
What sets the archetype apart from others on the same equipment (the second part of the identifier); blank when nothing does.
Variant tags that end the identifier: an efficiency step (efficiency-moderate, efficiency-strong), a capture variant (ccs-concentrated, ccs-diffuse) or a fuel or heating change.

conventional (the incumbent in Canadian plants), efficient variant, alternative (commercial but not common in Canada), prospective (technology readiness level 5-8), component or reference (kept for their numbers; not offered to the model).
The energy carriers the archetype can use.
The hierarchy nodes the archetype serves, or "no connection".
Technology readiness level, from 1 (basic principles observed) to 9 (proven in commercial operation).
The unit of output every cost and intensity is per.
The main product or service the product-unit counts.
Other useful outputs (co-products); costs are not split between them.
Density of the product, for converting between mass and volume.
Unit of product-density.
Energy content of the product (higher heating value), for converting between mass or volume and energy.
Unit of product-energy-content.
Number of source examples mapped to the archetype.
quantified (at least one value from a source) or estimated (every value filled by a rule or a judgement).
Short names of the sources behind the examples.

Parameters whose pooled value rests on a conversion factor from outside the source (a heating value, a density, a process ratio, a pooled efficiency, or an assumption), as examples so converted / examples pooled. Those values are shaded as converted in the workbook (see readme). Which factors: archetype-parameter.csv (external-factors); how each example was converted: example-parameter.csv (conversion, conversion-class, conversion-factors).

Parameters whose pooled value includes a figure the source prints wrongly and the modeller corrected (a slipped decimal or zero, a wrong unit or carrier label), as examples so corrected / examples pooled. Each correction, the figure as printed, and the evidence: records/reference/source-correction.csv; the rows carry the correction-id in example-parameter.csv (correction) and a note starting ASSUMED CORRECTION. These values are also counted in external-conversions and shaded as converted in the workbook (see readme).

Parameters with no sourced value, filled by the fill step and graded: identity (calculated from this archetype's own values), estimated (from other archetypes or a class rule fitted on this database), proxy (a class constant from a named outside catalogue, records/fill/fill-assumption.csv) or guess (a judgement, records/fill/fill-judgement.csv); not-applicable marks a parameter that does not characterise the archetype. Shaded by grade in the workbook (see readme); their _n is 0. Rule, inputs, and rationale: archetype-parameter.csv (grade, method, rule-id, inputs, rationale); rules in records/fill/.
